title: Consent request object
description: The one request object produced by both entry points and fetched by the authenticator over its authenticated channel. The binding code is deliberately absent: the authenticator never displays it (rule 2). The `client` object has two shapes: protocol 1.1 (the only shape implementations produce) names a client by its fingerprint and, when proven, its domain; the 1.0 shape with an operator-asserted name is accepted so that 1.0 requests keep validating.

binding_message.description: As it will be rendered and signed: the empty string for step-up entry and for a client without a proven domain.

expiry.description: Unix time in seconds after which the request is void.

bound_hash.description: group_hash or request_hash the consent is bound to.

sub.description: Pairwise subject of the requesting client.

v1_0.title: Protocol 1.0 rule: a 1.0 client that was not verified has no text channel

clientV1_1.title: Requesting client, protocol 1.1
clientV1_1.description: Biatec OIDC vouches for no client. The user sees the proven domain, or "Unproven application" with the fingerprint, never a name taken from the operator or from the client.

fingerprint.description: 8 lowercase hex characters of the SHA-256 of the client_id, shown as xxxx-xxxx.

domain_proven.description: True when the client proved control of its domain by serving /.well-known/biatec-client.json that lists its client_id.

domain.description: The proven domain in ASCII (A-label) form. Present exactly when domain_proven is true.

linked.description: Whether this user already linked this client on their phone (first use of any client always asks).

entity_id.description: OpenID Federation entity identifier, or client_id when the client has none.

verified.description: True only when the entity statement chains to a recognized trust anchor.

fingerprint.description: Short client_id fingerprint shown for unverified clients.
